key_insight: Wildfire-SSR combines satellite imagery and street-view evidence to assess wildfire vulnerability at the individual-structure level. Its geolocation-aware approach connects broad geographic context with local details that may influence ignition risk.
problem_solved: Existing wildfire assessment methods struggle to capture parcel-scale ignition pathways while maintaining community-wide geographic coverage.
method: Use satellite imagery to capture macro-scale geographic context.
Incorporate street-view imagery to provide micro-scale evidence about individual structures and their surroundings.
Apply geolocation-aware multimodal fusion; the abstract also mentions a vision-language model, but is truncated before describing its extraction targets.
impact: The framework illustrates how complementary imagery sources can support fine-grained environmental risk assessment. It offers AI/ML practitioners a multimodal design direction, although the supplied abstract does not report performance results.
visual_elements: Two-scale diagram linking a satellite neighborhood view to a street-level structure view.
Fusion pipeline showing satellite imagery, street-view imagery, and geolocation feeding a structure-level assessment.
Conceptual community map with individual buildings colored by illustrative vulnerability levels.
Zoom-in graphic connecting community-scale context to parcel-scale ignition pathways.
paper_title: Wildfire-SSR: Geolocation-Aware Multimodal Fusion for Structure-Level Wildfire Risk Assessment
paper_authors: Yu-Hsuan Ho, Yiming Xiao, Hao-En Lai, Ali Mostafavi, Samuel D. Brody
